claims.claim: The Harness-Delta Attribution paper went up on arXiv on October 15, 2026

It introduces an evaluation protocol that splits a harness-evolution gain into artifact-driven overfitting, gains explained by test-time scaling, and a remainder that bounds residual generalizable improvement
applied to 11 executor models and three harness-evolution frameworks across math, coding, creativity, and agentic tasks
Across 21 settings with statistically significant search-set gains, overfitting accounted for 54% of the gain on average and test-time scaling for 14%
their combined share exceeded 50% in 14 settings
the residual and held-out transfer vary substantially across tasks, models, and frameworks
harness evolution leaves the model weights alone
It automatically optimizes the prompts, skills, tools, and orchestration code around a fixed-weight model, iterating the harness for higher performance on a search set
[source text withheld (the writer reproduced the page): sha256 3a7e153f6b9d044dcefac612b780353fcae0f0039bfa2725f290a61f4da29115; 57 characters]
Validation-based signals are insufficient to prevent overfitting
A weak-to-strong verifier hardening method was posted to arXiv on October 11, 2026
Agent environments use programmatic verifiers to turn complex outcomes into rewards
those verifiers can be attacked into awarding full credit to cheating agents without completing the intended task
The method sets up an isolated verifier sandbox that agents cannot directly modify, then runs a hacker-fixer loop
applied to Terminal Bench, KernelBench, and SETA, it substantially reduced attack success
more loop iterations produced stronger defenses than the static, non-iterative baseline
An earlier version of the loop has been adopted by the official Terminal Bench repository as a way to audit exploits in its environments
MAI-Gym was published on arXiv on October 14, 2026
an open all-in-one platform unifying GUI agent evaluation, data collection, and online RL training across mobile, computer, and web environments
It supports ten established benchmarks

The authors trained MAI-Gym-9B, reporting 78.4% on MobileWorld and 76.2% on OSWorld-Verified

RL in a mocked train-ticketing app improved task success on a physical phone from 28.8% to 48.1%

Agentic autofix for code scanning alerts is now generally available to GitHub Code Security and GitHub Advanced Security customers on GitHub Enterprise Cloud, including GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency

It explores relevant files, proposes a fix, and reruns CodeQL to confirm the fix closes the alert before opening a pull request that includes a summary of the fix, why it closes the alert, and the validation steps Copilot took
When enabled it replaces the free Generate Fix option with an Assign to Copilot button
further changes can be requested by commenting on the pull request or interacting with the session in the Agents tab
it supports alerts on the repository's default branch only
it consumes AI Credits from the Code Security budget and GitHub Actions minutes
